status_summary: On 2025-04-11 the Interior Solicitor's office issued opinion M-37085, repealing M-37065 and making the 2017 opinion M-37050, which reads the Act as not covering incidental take, binding on the Department, except for actions within the Southern District of New York, where a court vacated M-37050 in 2020. On 2025-04-21 FWS withdrew its 2021 advance notice on a permit program for incidental take, citing Secretary's Order 3418, and a May 2026 FWS presentation also lists rescission of Director's Order 225 among these steps. A Federal Register search found no rule reinstating the codified January 2021 definition, so the position rests on a reversible legal opinion rather than a rule.

timeline.event: Interior Solicitor's office issued M-37085, repealing M-37065 and treating M-37050 (no prohibition on incidental take) as binding on the Department.
FWS published withdrawal of the 2021 advance notice on authorizing incidental take of migratory birds, citing Secretary's Order 3418.

title: Reinstate the Trump-era Migratory Bird Treaty Act incidental take position
uncertainties: A Federal Register API search of FWS documents since 2025-01-20 found no rule reinstating the 2021 incidental take regulation or rescinding the October 2021 revocation; no lawsuit against M-37085 was found in a news search or in the Harvard tracker, which is used only as a lead and was last updated in July 2025. The FWS presentation is undated beyond May 2026 and gives no dates for the steps it lists.
